data.narrative:
Arbe Robotics is a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector that has raised $118M to date. The relevant peer universe consists of eight private companies operating in the same sector, including Joby Aviation, Archer Aviation, Waymo, Wayve, and Zipline. There are no public comparables in this narrowly defined space, limiting the availability of tradeable market signals.

Standard peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient clustering. The Drones & Autonomous sector contains seven same-sector peers overall, but applying filters for stage alignment and valuation-tier similarity yielded fewer than three datapoints—the minimum threshold for statistical reliability. A broader all-sector median approach would introduce material noise given the heterogeneity of business models and development timelines across autonomous systems.

The absence of both narrow-set peers and public comparables creates a structural challenge to conventional triangulation. Any valuation synthesis would rest on either: (1) single-company precedent transactions, if available; (2) discounted cash flow analysis anchored to technology adoption curves specific to drone/autonomous applications; or (3) venture capital market pricing for later-stage funding rounds. The primary uncertainty is determining which private peer most closely mirrors Arbe's technology maturity, addressable market, and path to profitability. Without sufficient comparable data, valuation estimates should be treated as highly model-dependent and sensitive to assumptions about autonomous systems commercialization timelines.
